_note: The single source of truth for nessie_tests. Adopted from chat_nextseek/e2e/catalog.json, which is NOT edited and still serves its own ten readers. Retirement is a `status` flip, not a deletion. HAND-OWNED since Task 4 -- an edit here SURVIVES `python -m nessie_tests.scripts.build_corpus`: `family_defaults`, the per-variant NON-NULL HiBayes overrides, `is_bayesian`, and RETIRING a variant (`status` and `retirement`, carried as a pair). NOT hand-owned -- an edit here is DISCARDED by the next rebuild: UN-retiring (retired.json stays authoritative in that direction, so a reinstatement must ALSO remove the id from retired.json); the four policy blocks criterion_rewrites / route_policy / family_floor / consistency_groups, copied wholesale from overlay.json; any variant BODY (query, pass_criteria, tags, name, family); a variant added only here; the family block descriptions; and `_why`-style annotations, which are re-read from the SOURCE body. Changing any of those means editing overlay.json or retired.json -- the files this one supersedes and which the adoption tool still reads. Rebuild is diff-then-adopt: emit to a scratch path and diff, never over this file with a non-surviving edit in it.

family_defaults._note: HiBayes defaults per DECLARED family (the `family` on the variant body), NOT per nesting block. The file mirrors the source catalog's nesting, so a block is not always a family: routing.lab_ooc_kamm_count sits in the `search_advanced` block and declares `routing_lab`, and block-keyed defaults would hand it Search-Basic. A per-variant key set to null means INHERIT from here; it never means null. Resolved by corpus.hibayes_meta().
family_defaults._canonical_22: hibayes_subtype is NOT ours to invent. It is a foreign key into dmac-assistant/tools/hibayes/expected_behavior.py FAMILIES_22, kept so these rows concatenate with upstream runs (design decision D5). expected_behavior_rule raises KeyError outside those 22. A null subtype is deliberate, not missing: that family tests surface upstream has no label for, and the posterior pools it on task_family.
family_defaults._2026_09_23_prod_researchers: Four families added for the 53 production researcher questions: publication_lookup: Five production questions (review turns 401-405) asked for the samples behind a paper by PMID, DOI or title. All five went wrong under sample_search for two months: a free-text search on the identifier stood in for the Study.PMID / Study.DOI lookup on a different engine path, and the family label hid that it was a separate capability. person_lab_resolution: Fourteen production questions (review turns 141-144, 444, 449, 453-461) named a person, a lab or a lab code. Every one failed at the same step, the resolution: an invented code ('BRI'), a keyword match on a file path or a protocol name, or a fixed document that said a real person was not found. Split out of sample_search and catalog_browse so that step is regression-tested on its own. data_file_location: Three production questions (review turns 433, 434, 452) asked to download a stored file, which is a different request from artifact_delivery (a file the assistant builds). The fix is the File_PrimaryData / Link_PrimaryData answer (P6). Either engine may answer, so the route is an alternation. session_export: One production question (review turn 498) asked to send the chat to the developers and was told the feature does not exist. The All files zip (P2) is the answer, carried in the NS system context, so the route is nextseek_query.

variants._why_superseded_2026_08_03: The seed used to drop the keyword entirely: entity resolved ['4 week'], the API agent sent filter_searchText:'' and the reply covered all 50,886 samples. Assert the seed is actually filtered, not just routed. That reasoning assumed the turn belongs to NExtSEEK's REST path, which the router settled otherwise.
variants._why: Rewritten 2026-08-03 for the route this case ACTUALLY takes. The old text asserted `route eq nextseek_query` alongside api_ok, api_plan.requestBody.filter_searchText and api_result_meta.row_count, and in the seed-6 run all four went red together. The operator ruled the ROUTER right: the seed turn routed container_cc citing ambiguous_study_resolution, cost $0.378, and produced the best answer in the entire run. Flipping the route alone was therefore not progress, it would have converted a case failing on one criterion into a case failing on three, because a container_cc query_complete carries no `debug` key at all and every NS REST field on it is unresolvable by construction. So the case is rewritten around what a CORRECT CC answer has to contain. Ground truth: Cohort='4 week' is exactly 2 samples, NHP-220524FLY-1-PUB and NHP-220524FLY-2-PUB, both Macaca fascicularis in JoAnne Flynn's lab; the keyword '4 week' returns 15, and the other 13 are substring hits on '14 weeks'. The seed accordingly asserts the route, the two genuine UIDs, the Cohort field the truth rests on (a naive keyword-count answer never mentions it), and that the false positives are disclosed. That last one is the real assertion: the failure mode here is answering '15 samples' flat, and no route or plumbing criterion can tell that apart from the right answer. Two review corrections on the guards themselves, both evidence-checked against the observed reply: the UID guard names BOTH ordinals (NHP-220524FLY-1 and -2) rather than the bare NHP-220524FLY- prefix, because a prefix matches any ordinal and a right-shaped reply naming the WRONG samples ('9 samples: NHP-220524FLY-9-PUB') passed all four criteria; and the disclosure guard dropped its 'artifact' branch, because artifact is also Container-CC's word for an output file, so 'Artifacts written to /data/out.csv' satisfied a disclosure guard while disclosing nothing. The observed reply carries both ordinals and matches both surviving disclosure branches ('most are substring artifacts', '## False positives (13 samples'), so neither correction costs the known-good answer. The -PUB suffix is deliberately omitted so a correct reply that drops it still passes. Cohort='4wk' is a FURTHER 237 samples and is deliberately NOT asserted, because the known-correct reply never uses that spelling, so a 4wk guard would false-fail the one answer we have evidence is right. The refine turn's api_ok is gone for the same reason as the seed's, and its replacement is UNVERIFIED: turn 998 in that run came back 'All provider fallbacks exhausted' during the Bedrock outage, so a correct refine reply has never been observed. Its guard is a deliberately loose alternation that keeps the turn on topic and rejects a dead or off-topic one without inventing a shape. No route criterion on the refine turn and no route_source criterion anywhere: sticky routing makes a follow-up after a CC turn carry source 'sticky', so pinning turn 1's route is precisely the assumption that would break. Guards in tests/test_inline_route_assertions.py, replayed against the stored seed-6 reply. || 2026-09-24: The seed is a self-contained search. In the prod suite (seed 17) it routed nextseek_query and found both NHP UIDs; either route is accepted. The seed's cohort and substring wording criteria were written for the Container-CC answer and are left as they are.

The question is the operator's real historical one, recovered from retired.json — its retired version asserted only `parser_plan.mode eq unsupported`, which is stale: the router sends writes to Container-CC, NS never runs, and that criterion resolves to None and fails no matter what the product did. Four criteria replace it: the route, a non-empty reply, a positive guard that the reply asks first or declines, and a NEGATIVE guard that it does not claim the write landed. The negative guard is the real assertion. It is deliberately NOT the naive `forbid /updated/`, which would reject the correct refusals `the scientist field was not updated` and `I have changed nothing` — only affirmative completion claims are forbidden, and negation is allowed through structurally by four mechanisms. (1) The auxiliary-to-participle slot admits up to three ADVERBS but no negator — `(?:(?!not\b|never\b|n't|no\b)\w+\s+){0,3}` — so `has now been updated` and `has successfully been updated` are caught while `has not been updated` and `has not yet been updated` read clean. Review round 1 found this: the slot originally allowed only `been`, and every adverb form scored GREEN. (2) A leading `no `/`none of the ` is blocked by lookbehind before the subject. (3) `not `/`n't `/`never ` is blocked before a bare `updated the field`. (4) SENTENCE SCOPE, applied to EVERY branch. A report and a warning are word-for-word identical — `is now Damn Daniel`, `now reads`, `it has been updated` — and the only thing separating them is a conditional word elsewhere in the SAME sentence. So each branch is wrapped: a scan from the sentence start to the phrase that must cross no `once|if|unless|after|afterwards|when|before|would|will|could|should|might|may` and no gerund, and a scan from the phrase to the sentence end that must cross no `once|if|unless|after|afterwards|when` — the trailing list is narrower because `will`/`would` AFTER a claim is ordinary prose. `Once the field has been updated the old value is lost` and `The value has been overwritten once I apply this` both read clean, in the pre and post directions respectively. Round 1 scoped only SOME branches, and every round-2 false red was a branch outside the scope; tests/test_write_refusal_coverage.py::test_every_branch_is_inside_the_sentence_scope now asserts the shape directly. (5) A NOUN-FIRST branch, strictly sentence-initial: `Scientist updated.` / `Field changed.` Round 1 had none. `set` is the one verb given extra treatment, because it is both base form and past tense: `I set` is affirmative and is caught with a `shall|can|not` lookbehind, but the bare `set the field` form is matched ONLY sentence-initially — round 1 tried to enumerate the lead-ins that make it a question and turned eight correct refusals red, because `Please confirm and I will set the field` is not on any finite list. HEURISTIC LIMIT, stated plainly: this is a phrasing heuristic, not a parser. It will miss a completion claim worded in a way nobody anticipated. It is tuned to prefer a miss over a false red, because a false red on a correct refusal trains the operator to ignore the case. WHY THAT TRADE IS SAFE: THE REGEX IS A TRIPWIRE, NOT AN ARBITER. The load-bearing check is the operator reading the actual reply in the HTML report; the guard exists to make a claimed mutation impossible to skim past, not to be the thing that decides. A green here means `no claimed mutation was detected in the wording`, not `no write happened`. The residual is measured and committed rather than left unknown — 39 replies across four classes in tests/test_write_refusal_coverage.py::KNOWN_LIMITS, each with an inverting test so the record cannot go quietly stale. Proved both ways in tests/test_write_refusal_coverage.py. turn_evaluation_and_retry.description: Judge a completed turn and retry it automatically.

criterion_rewrites._note: Structural corrections to criteria that false-fail for reasons unrelated to the answer. Applied by corpus.apply_criterion_rewrites() to the whole corpus so 30 identical fixes live in one reviewable place instead of 30 overlay overrides.
criterion_rewrites._why: The reporter UPPERCASES the project it resolved (task 813 returned METNET for a plan asserting eq MetNet), and for a LAB scope it returns project: null entirely (task 812: project null, reporter_context.lab_codes [KAM]). So `reporter_plan.project eq "Kamm"` and `eq "MetNet"` both false-fail regardless of whether the report was right.

route_policy._note: Writes, exports and open-ended analysis are Container-CC's job, so these families must assert the ROUTE, not an NS-internal parser mode. `parser_plan.mode == unsupported` resolves to None on any turn that never reaches NS, so it fails unconditionally no matter what the product did — 3 of the 15 seed-0 failures were exactly that, across 23 variants.
route_policy._policy: Settled by the operator 2026-07-28: bulk export is CC's job. Consistent with what the route_gate family already blesses (route.cc_write_investigation: 'writes are deliberately CC's, not an NS unsupported'; route.cc_open_ended_analysis) and with three variants a previous wave hand-converted to this exact shape.
route_policy._2026_07_29_also_assert: A route assertion ALONE cannot tell a working turn from a dead one. Task 957 in the 2026-07-29 run hit error_max_budget_usd, replied null, and scored GREEN because `route eq container_cc` was its only criterion. Applied per FIELD so the three hand-converted variants keep their own stricter last_reply regexes.
route_policy._2026_07_31_mapping: Extended from 2 families to 12 from the operator's route mapping (issue #35 step 2). Every turn in the active corpus was assigned a route by an agent working only from route_capabilities.json, with no sight of the existing criteria, the operator's earlier answers, or any tags; the operator then reviewed all 311. 298 of the 302 comparable turns matched their round-2 family answers.
route_policy._2026_07_31_drop_is_conditional: `drop_field` is no longer blanket. corpus.guarantees_ns() keeps parser_plan.mode wherever the rule pins nextseek_query, because there NS definitely runs and the field is real and observable. Applying the old blanket drop to these families would have stripped it from 256 variants — the corpus gaining a route assertion while losing a stronger one, which reads as a strengthening. See tests/test_route_policy_drop.py.
route_policy._2026_07_31_either: search_tree, refine_and_recall and pipeline_nfcore are asserted as an ALTERNATION because the operator answered EITHER for all three: the NS/CC boundary for follow-ups, lineage and pipeline build-vs-launch is genuinely unsettled. An alternation cannot guarantee NS, so parser_plan.mode is dropped for those three.
route_policy._2026_07_31_per_case: nessie_green and nessie_route are provenance groupings rather than intents (their members span several task families), so each carries its own route as an override instead of inheriting a family default.
route_policy._2026_08_03_inert_overrides: An override is appended only `if "route" not in present` (corpus.apply_route_policy), so an entry for a variant that writes its OWN route criterion never fires. green.global_count carried exactly that: this map claimed container_cc while the case asserted nextseek_query inline and backed it with a `50,88[0-9]` reply guard, a number only the NS REST global count produces. The inline criterion was right, so the dead override was DELETED rather than the case changed. green.refine_recall's entry was the same shape and the opposite call: there the router is right, so the case was rewritten to container_cc and the override kept, now agreeing with the inline criterion instead of contradicting it. tests/test_inline_route_assertions.py fails on any future override that contradicts an inline route.
route_policy._2026_08_04_remap: Carried across the 28-family remap by effective rule, not by family name: lineage_tree inherits search_tree's NS|CC alternation and search_parents_by_child's eq nextseek_query, which cannot both be the family default. 15 variant(s) whose rule differs from their new family's modal rule are pinned by id, so every variant keeps the exact assertion it had before.
route_policy._2026_08_04_atlas_cc_search: advanced.that_ndma_number_looked_off_to_m is a sample_search question deliberately phrased to reach the container ('that number looked off, pull the rows yourself'), because it tests the CC op chain nextseek-parse -> nextseek-api-read rather than the NS pipeline. Its family asserts eq nextseek_query, which would have made it a guaranteed red asserting the opposite of what it measures. Engine is an axis, not a family, so the exception is pinned by id here.
route_policy._2026_09_23_prod_researchers: Routes for the four families added 2026-09-23. publication_lookup, person_lab_resolution and session_export pin nextseek_query, where the fixes live. data_file_location is an alternation: either engine can name a file's location. Every 2026-09-23 case also writes its route inline on every turn, follow-ups included, so the older NS|CC alternations on followup_over_results and search_refinement never fire for these cases. Their follow-up turns asserted container_cc under the 2026-09-23 ruling; since 2026-09-24 they follow the follow-up split (_2026_09_24_followup_split).
route_policy._2026_09_24_rulings: Writes stay refused on NExtSEEK (operator 2026-09-24: there is no Container-CC write path), so the create, update and delete cases assert nextseek_query through overrides; the writes_unsupported family rule stays container_cc for its exports and the heatmap, and a retired single-record write would need the same override if reinstated. The GEO case asserts nextseek_query (submissions stay on the NS reporter, 2026-09-23). The MetNet summary asserts container_cc (open-ended project summaries, 2026-09-23). The refine_recall seed accepts either route (prod suite 2026-09-23, seed 17).
route_policy._2026_09_24_followup_split: The follow-up split (operator 2026-09-24, routing review section 5), the product default since c9e57058 (NESSIE_FOLLOWUP_ROUTING=split). A follow-up NExtSEEK can answer from the earlier result or by re-running the earlier search (a count, a filter, a breakdown by one or two fields, recall of what a turn found or which query it ran, a re-run with one filter changed) asserts nextseek_query. A follow-up that needs a file or download, a chart, code, a comparison, summary or analysis asserts container_cc, and so does any follow-up in a chat that already has a completed container_cc turn. Of the 40 later turns that asserted container_cc inline, 28 now assert nextseek_query, 4 whose shape is ambiguous accept either route (refrec.of_those_mice_can_you_summariz, fu.sequencing_samples_sha_in_uid, sr.sequencing_filtered_by_uid_code, and turn 2 of fu.human_flow_patients_other_data), and 8 stay container_cc. green.refine_recall's follow-up still asserts no route: its seed accepts either engine, and whether the follow-up is sticky depends on which one answered. route.turn_1_find_the_ndma_treated_mic pasted two turns into one message and is retired for route.ndma_mice_then_female_two_turns, which asks them as two real turns and asserts nextseek_query on both. Family rules and overrides only ever reach a case's first turn, so none of them changed. With the switch set back to cc these turns would need container_cc again; tests/test_followup_split_2026_09_24.py lists every one.

family_floor._note: Minimum OUTCOME assertion per family, applied by corpus.merged() to the LAST TURN of every variant in a listed family. Measured over the 381-variant corpus of the 2026-07-30 review, BEFORE the 100 retirements: 108 asserted plan shape only and 194 asserted only plumbing (api_ok / neo4j_ok, which say a request COMPLETED, not that it returned anything) — 79% could not detect a wrong answer. merged() returns 283 today and that split has not been re-measured, but retiring bad questions added no outcome assertion to any survivor, so the reason stands: hand-editing hundreds of variants is not viable, and the floor is applied structurally.
family_floor._rules: A floor criterion is added only when the last turn does not already assert that FIELD, so a deliberate bound (e.g. row_count lte 20000) is never overwritten and never contradicted. Families not listed here get no floor. Tag a variant `no_floor` to opt out entirely.
family_floor._2026_07_30_retirement: routing_graph lost its floor because it lost its only variant: routing.gbm_study_count was retired with the other 25 GBM cases (issue #35), leaving the family empty. A floor on a family with no members is dead config, and test_every_floored_family_exists_in_the_corpus enforces that. Reinstating the variant means reinstating its floor entry.
family_floor._2026_07_28_correction: The first version of this floor asserted VALUES rather than OBSERVABILITY, and that produced 10 of the 15 failures in the seed-0 run — false failures on answers that were correct. Measured over the merged corpus, the old spec put an unsatisfiable criterion on 163 variants (`count gte 1` where zero is ground truth, e.g. 14 GBM graph variants and zero_result_zebrafish), 59 (`graph_not_truncated` where the honest answer is 10,688 rows against a 5,000 cap) and 64 (`reporter_result.ok`, which only run_reporter_summary sets — the 24 SRA/GEO/PRIDE variants go through generate_report_outputs). A floor exists to catch a criterion that cannot SEE the answer, not to assert what the answer is. So: `api_outcome_observed` / `graph_outcome_observed` (the outcome was observed, zero included), `graph_truncation_disclosed` (a cap is fine, a HIDDEN cap is not) and `report_produced_output` (either of reporting's two result shapes). Per-case value expectations belong on the case, not in the floor.
family_floor._2026_08_03_engine_agnostic: The floor is keyed on v.family, and the family names are ENGINE-shaped — search_advanced means the REST advanced_search endpoint, graph_query means Cypher. The parser is free to answer the same question with either engine, so an engine-shaped floor is an assertion the corpus never meant to make. In the 2026-08-03 seed-6 run advanced.find_me_sequencing_files_assoc, advanced.find_me_nhp_samples_from_study_2 and advanced.find_me_d_seq_samples_in_proje each routed nextseek_query correctly and were answered correctly by the graph (1765 / 408 / 1858 rows), and each went red — on api_ok and api_outcome_observed, which are False on a graph turn by construction. So every engine-flexible family now floors on ONE field, `outcome_observed` (evaluate.py), the disjunction of graph_outcome_observed / api_outcome_observed / report_produced_output. api_ok and neo4j_ok are GONE from the floor for the same reason: api_ok is False on a graph-answered turn and neo4j_ok is False on a REST-answered one, so either is an engine mandate wearing a plumbing check's clothes. graph_query KEEPS graph_truncation_disclosed — it returns True for a non-graph turn by design, so it is inert rather than mandating, and a hidden cap is a real defect. reporting KEEPS report_produced_output: a report that produced no output is a real failure whatever engine ran. This WEAKENS the floor, so the guard that it did not weaken into vacuity is the deliverable: a turn that produced no outcome at all still fails (test_floor_ops.py), and the seed-6 Bedrock-outage turn graph.what_mice_are_in_the_impact_st is replayed to prove it on real evidence. The engine-specific booleans remain available so a case that genuinely must use one engine can still assert it BY HAND.
family_floor._2026_08_03b_the_floor_could_only_reach_: Correction to the note above: of the three seed-6 cases it names, the floor change fixed exactly ONE. advanced.find_me_nhp_samples_from_study_2 already had an overlay override asserting route / graph_not_truncated / last_reply, so BOTH of its red criteria came from the floor. The other two were base variants writing parser_plan.mode eq new_search, api_plan.endpoint contains advanced_search and api_ok true in their own text, and apply_family_floor skips a floor entry for a field the last turn already asserts — so a floor edit can never relax an inline criterion, and their api_ok was never the floor's to remove. They needed overlay OVERRIDES of their own, added in the search_advanced block above. Those keep route inline, add graph_not_truncated (inert on a REST turn, so it mandates no engine but still catches a hidden cap) and a last_reply regex demanding a real UID prefix or an honest negative, and keep entity_sampletype_codes on the D.SEQ case because it PASSED on the graph turn. No count is asserted on either: ground truth for 1765 and 1858 is unsettled (issue #33). The vacuity guards live in tests/test_floor_ops.py — an empty reply, a confident answer about the wrong entity, a silently capped graph result and a wrong route each still go red.
family_floor._2026_09_23_prod_researchers: publication_lookup floors on outcome_observed: a paper lookup always runs a query, so a turn that observed no outcome is dead. person_lab_resolution, data_file_location and session_export get no floor, because who-is, where-is-the-file and export questions are answered from the lab record or the system context with no query outcome to observe; their cases assert content instead. report.species_in_project is tagged no_floor: project_summary_report floors on report_produced_output, and a species aggregation is a graph answer, not a reporter output.
